transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I keep catching myself having these thoughts lately. Like, I just keep thinking it might be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. I mean, I haven't made any actual plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But it's happening enough that I figured I should probably come in and talk to somebody about it.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

I don't think so. I mean... everyone gets down sometimes, but actually thinking about not waking up? No, I'm pretty sure this is the first time it's been like this. At least, I don't remember ever feeling quite this way before.
Did anything specific happen in your life around the time these thoughts began?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I'm just working my regular shifts at the store, doing the usual routine. Nothing bad happened, no big life changes or anything like that. It just sort of... crept up on me, I guess. I can't really point to any one thing that set it off.
How much have these feelings been affecting your ability to get through your daily responsibilities at work or at home?

Well, it's definitely making things harder. I mean, I'm still showing up for my shifts at the store, but... outside of that, things are slipping. I fell behind on my bills recently, which isn't like me. And I've missed a few callbacks and appointments because I just couldn't get it together. I even tried looking for a second job because I need the extra money, but I couldn't keep a steady search going. Even my usual routines around the house have gotten pretty sloppy. It got bad enough that I finally realized I couldn't just push through it with willpower anymore.
How has your sleep been lately?

Not great, honestly. Um... even when I do actually get to sleep now, I end up waking up way before daylight. And the second my eyes open, my stomach is just tight. My mind is already going, you know, just immediately thinking about the bills and what I messed up. It's just hard to get any real rest.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely taken a hit. Most days lately, I honestly have to remind myself to eat. When I do try to have supper, it just sits there on the plate looking like too much trouble to even chew. I haven't weighed myself, but my jeans are definitely fitting looser than they usually do, so I must be dropping some weight.
Do you feel like you are moving and speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, do you feel so restless that you cannot sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm pretty tired from not sleeping, but I don't think I'm talking slow or moving like molasses or anything. And I'm not pacing around or feeling like I can't sit still, either. I guess physically, I'm just moving around about the same as I always do.
Are you still finding enjoyment or pleasure in the activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I kind of just quit caring about the things that usually settle me down. Like, I used to go fishing, or I'd spend time digging through vinyl records, tailgating, even checking on my home-brew. But lately... I don't know, doing any of that just feels like a chore. I don't get anything out of it right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, let's see... it's been about three months now. Ever since that crash, this low spell has just been hanging on.
You mentioned a crash earlier; could you tell me a little more about what you meant by that?

Well, before this low period started, I had this... this big burst of energy. But then it just wore off. It felt like somebody had just pulled the plug on me. After that, I'd just sit at the kitchen table, staring at my coffee, feeling completely empty. And... I don't know, just really ashamed, I guess. That's what I mean by the crash.
During that time when you had that big burst of energy, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual, and did that period last for at least four days?

Yeah, that's exactly how it was. I mean, it definitely lasted longer than four days. There were several nights during that stretch where I only slept two, maybe three hours. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all. I'd get up feeling like I had a full tank of gas, just totally ready to go with no reason to slow down.
During that period of high energy, did your behavior become so intense or unusual that it caused significant problems for you at work or with your friends and family?

Yeah, it definitely caused some issues. I ended up falling way behind on my bills. I was missing callbacks and... well, appointments I had scheduled. I really needed work at the time, but I just couldn't keep a steady job search going. 

And around the house, my usual routines just got really sloppy. It got bad enough that I finally realized I couldn't just handle it by willpower anymore, you know?
During that high-energy period, was your behavior ever so extreme that you required hospitalization or experienced a break from reality, such as hearing or seeing things that weren't there?

I didn't go to the hospital, no. But about hearing things... yeah, actually, I did. When I was all wound up like that, I heard my old store manager's voice. It sounded clear as day, like it was coming right over a store intercom, telling me to 'move the display.' 

The thing is, I was just sitting completely alone in my kitchen when it happened. There wasn't any intercom or anyone else around. So, yeah, I guess that would be a break from reality.
